summary: Tested new Appointments feature (backend + frontend) for Óptica Ari. All 16 backend tests passed (100%). Frontend booking flow at /citas works end-to-end (service select → date → slot → form → POST 200 → confirmation screen with WhatsApp link). Admin /admin Citas tab loads, lists appointments including the freshly created one, status dropdown triggers PUT 200. Delete uses an icon button (no 'Eliminar' text) — backend DELETE was verified via pytest.

issues: Calendar opens at current month and disables all past days correctly, but there is no automatic jump to the next month if the current month has no available days — user must manually click ›. Minor UX nit, not a blocker.

critical_code_review_comments: _generate_slots() loop logic is convoluted; could be replaced with a simple range-based generator. Currently produces 20 slots (9:00–14:00 inclusive, 15:00–19:00 inclusive) — matches spec.
POST /appointments has no rate limiting and is unauthenticated — consider adding a captcha or per-IP throttle to prevent spam booking.
Admin delete button in AdminDashboardPage.jsx uses an icon without data-testid — recommend adding data-testid='delete-appt-{id}' for testability.
Admin status dropdown also lacks data-testid; rows lack identifiable testids.
seed_data_creation: Created appointment for TEST_UI_Cliente on 2026-05-04 19:00 via UI; backend pytest creates and cleans up its own appointments. The UI-created one (TEST_UI_Cliente) remains in DB unless deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Container clock is around April 30, 2026. Calendar starts at current month (April 2026) so for May tests the › button must be clicked. Use data-testid selectors: service-{name}, cal-day-YYYY-MM-DD, slot-HH:MM. Admin tab labeled 'Citas (n)' inside /admin. To clean up, login as admin and delete TEST_UI_Cliente row, or call DELETE /api/admin/appointments/{id}.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. Backend endpoints conform to spec (services count, availability slots, Sunday closed, 409 conflicts, 400 invalid inputs, admin auth gates). Frontend booking and admin management flows integrate correctly with backend.
